html:
This territory marks the lands in southwestern Oklahoma shared by the Kiowa, Comanche and Plains Apache. The map shows it in 1492, but the area is defined by a later treaty.

These peoples ruled the southern Plains on horseback in the 1700s and 1800s. In the Medicine Lodge Treaty of 1867 they agreed to a joint reservation here, in return for much larger lands. The Comanche leader Quanah Parker later lived on it. In 1901 the US opened most of it to white settlers by lottery. The Kiowa chief Lone Wolf sued, and in 1903 the Supreme Court ruled that Congress could break Indian treaties on its own.
